Current research in microbial sciences 2026-12-01 Medium

Ultra-deep HiFi sequencing reveals rare structural-variant subpopulations in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from an LVAD-associated infection.

This study applies ultra-deep HiFi long-read sequencing to a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate from a left ventricular assist device (LVAD)-associated infection, revealing rare structural-variant subpopulations within the bacterial population. The work demonstrates that deep long-read sequencing can uncover within-host genomic heterogeneity that standard sequencing would miss, with implications for understanding antibiotic and phage resistance.

Zoological research 2026-11-18 Medium

From expression profiling to functional validation: evidence hierarchy and biomarker readiness of circular RNAs in aquatic animals.

This review surveys circular RNAs in aquatic animals, cataloging how high-throughput sequencing has expanded their known roles in growth, reproduction, immunity, and stress responses. It proposes an evidence hierarchy for moving from expression profiling to functional validation and assesses how ready circRNAs are as biomarkers in these species.

Cancer science 2026-11-16 Medium

MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.

MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of existing tools that ignore clinical context. This integration aims to improve the accuracy of variant interpretation in comprehensive genomic profiling for precision oncology.

Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology 2026-11-12 Medium

Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.

This review discusses DNAzyme-based biosensors as a promising approach for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. The authors argue that these catalytic DNA sensors offer advantages over conventional genotyping methods, which often require sophisticated instrumentation and struggle with complex biological samples, by combining programmable nucleic acid recognition with isothermal catalytic signal amplification.

Genome research 2026-11-10 Medium

Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.

The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variants directly from sequencing reads using locality-sensitive bucketing and k-mer counting instead of traditional read alignment. This approach enables ultrafast SNP detection and scales to massive viral sequencing datasets where alignment-based pipelines become computationally prohibitive.

The Journal of infectious diseases 2026-11-10 Medium

O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.

This study re-examined the capsule polysaccharides of pneumococcal serogroup 15 and found that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the serotype 15A capsule, not just the previously recognized 15A/15F pair. The work shows that conventional serological and molecular typing can miss O-acetylation-based capsule variation, which matters because 15A is included in newer conjugate vaccines.

Leveraging artificial intelligence for livestock genetics and breeding.

This review examines how artificial intelligence tools are currently being applied to livestock genetics and breeding, noting that while animal breeding has long used data-driven prediction, modern AI methods are still at an early stage. The authors highlight substantial potential for AI to improve genetic evaluation, selection decisions, and breeding programs for milk, meat, and egg production.

Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.

This study systematically evaluates and optimizes each step of a long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes from gut samples. The authors identify workflow choices that meaningfully affect assembly contiguity and genome completeness, and propose an integrated experimental-computational pipeline. The result is a practical framework for researchers seeking high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes from long-read data.

Journal of proteome research 2026-11-06 Medium

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass exopolysaccharide from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus that contains an uncommon pyruvylated GalNAc-Gal motif. Using proteomics-guided analysis of the strain's expressed proteins during growth on EPSLp, they identified candidate carbohydrate-active enzymes responsible for degrading this rare structure. This work expands knowledge of the enzymatic machinery for processing non-canonical, modified bacterial polysaccharides.

Genome biology and evolution 2026-11-05 Medium

Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.

The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male-female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics, addressing the field's overreliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, making it a useful outgroup for comparative studies.

Molecular plant 2026-11-04 Medium

Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can support predictive plant breeding by integrating genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data with scientific literature. It surveys applications across knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and intelligent breeding design, and includes a systematic evidence audit of the claims made for these technologies. The authors highlight both the capabilities and the current gaps in evidence for adopting these tools in breeding practice.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.

The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves Z-DNA-forming region detection by combining a permissive scan (broad candidate capture) with a stringent scan (high-confidence support) and integrating results through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan recall-rescue strategy aims to overcome the sensitivity-specificity trade-off in sequence-based Z-DNA prediction while remaining fast and interpretable.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under the Mendelian randomization principle, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographic factors. Existing methods struggle with such high-dimensional confounders, so this work aims to provide more robust causal network inference for genomic trio data.

Microbial genomics 2026-11-01 Medium

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by matching degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements even when they lack methicillin resistance genes. This fills a gap for studying the full diversity of these mobile genetic elements beyond just methicillin resistance.

Environmental microbiology 2026-11-01 Medium

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study systematically tested whether metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from bacterial genomes alone. Comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors found that prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, especially for simple substrates. The results caution against assuming that genome-based metabolic predictions are broadly reliable.

JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health 2026-11-01 Medium

Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.

This study used long-read sequencing to overcome the difficulty of characterizing the repetitive exon 3 of the FLG gene, revealing extensive copy number variation and enabling detection of rare loss-of-function variants. In a diverse cohort of 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, the authors identified both common and rare LOF variants associated with atopic dermatitis. The work demonstrates that long-read technology improves variant detection in this clinically important but technically challenging gene.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-10-31 Medium

Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a kidney-specific, cell-type-resolved manner, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and conditions. This provides a practical template for adapting general S2F models to specific tissues without training from scratch.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

The authors built a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to floatptosis, a newly described vacuolar cell death pathway triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. Using integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, they link these floatptosis-related genes to patient survival and immunotherapeutic features. The work is exploratory and the abstract is truncated, so the strength of the clinical claims remains unclear.

Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.

This study identifies cellular senescence-associated gene signatures through pan-cancer screening and builds a prognostic risk model for bladder urothelial carcinoma that integrates multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signals to tumor microenvironment features, aiming to connect molecular characterization with potential clinical translation.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software, which makes library design tedious and error-prone, and can also be used in silico to analyze genomic AI models.

Communications biology 2026-10-29 Medium

Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.

The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform built on Galaxy that bundles over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of microbial omics data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers for microbiologists working with metabarcoding, metagenomic, and metatranscriptomic data. The platform is globally accessible and maintained by the Galaxy and microbiology communities.

Nucleic acids research 2026-10-29 Medium

MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.

MitImpact 4 expands mitochondrial variant interpretation from the 13 protein-coding genes to the entire mitochondrial genome, covering all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants including tRNA and rRNA genes. This addresses a diagnostic blind spot where pathogenic variants in RNA genes were poorly served by computational predictors, providing functional consequence annotations genome-wide.

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) covering 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 variants with regulatory activity under FDR control. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer analogy. The work provides an experimentally grounded reference set for evaluating computational variant annotation.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the full workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. The system aims to streamline genome-guided natural product discovery.

Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model how read coverage varies across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and quantifies their usage across tissues, individuals, and disease states, revealing links between previously hidden processing patterns and disease risk.

Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.

SLCNV is a user-friendly Nextflow pipeline for detecting chromosomal copy number variation from low-pass whole genome sequencing data. It packages multiple copy number analyses into a single flexible workflow, lowering the computational barrier for wet-lab biologists who lack bioinformatics expertise.

Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.

This study uses computational approaches to identify MMP1 and MMP9 as potential molecular targets of the natural compounds curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma, then characterizes the structural basis of these interactions. cgMLST typing reproducibility is maintained across diverse whole-genome sequencing workflows in a multi-country HERA2 surveillance pilot.

This multi-country ring trial tested whether different laboratories' whole-genome sequencing workflows produce comparable cgMLST typing results for bacterial surveillance. Six labs in four European countries sequenced a standardized panel of 25 isolates from five public health-relevant species, and cgMLST-based interpretations remained reproducible across the heterogeneous workflows. The finding supports the robustness of cgMLST typing for routine cross-laboratory surveillance.

Survey of viruses associated with the whitefly Bemisia tabaci in cucurbits in Georgia, United States.

Researchers surveyed the virome of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) collected from cucurbit crops in Georgia over two years using RNA sequencing. Genomic profiling and drug resistance patterns of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Indonesia: whole-genome sequencing of isolates from the 2017-2018 national Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Survey.

This study used whole-genome sequencing to characterize Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Indonesia's 2017–2018 national drug resistance survey, mapping lineage distribution and genotypic resistance profiles across the archipelago.
